event.title: Research at Winterthur Speaker Series
event.description:
America’s First Woman Botanist

Jane Colden (1724–1760) was America’s first woman botanist, yet her contributions to the field of remain little-known and her writings are mostly unpublished. Enjoy this lecture restoring Colden’s life and work, in her own writings, her father’s correspondence, and botanic sources of the 18th century with Fenella Greig Heckscher, author of Jane Colden’s Botanic Manuscript: The Legacy of America’s First Woman Botanist. 

The Research at Winterthur series, presented by the Library, Research Fellowship Program, and Continuing Education, showcases new projects and publications that tap into our rich collections and resources, unveiling innovative perspectives for exploring the fascinating stories that objects can tell about people and our shared past. Registration required. Included with admission. Members free. Lecture followed by book signing.

Register now.

event.title: Stitched In Place: Needlework Conference
event.description:
March 19–21, 2027

Stitched in Place is a two-and-a-half-day conference that invites you to consider how place is not only a backdrop but a central thread in the story of American needlework. Join us to examine how Americans have used needlecraft and sewn and embroidered objects, whether stitched in schoolrooms, parlors, or workshops, to understand and communicate how they see the world and their places in it.

The conference will include research presentations, panel discussions, workshops for all interests and skill levels, special tours, and other exciting opportunities to engage with Winterthur’s extraordinary needlework collection.  

Participants will see behind-the-scenes in the Needlework Study room, visit our Textile Conservation Lab, learn how Winterthur protects and preserves its collections, and learn about scalable ways to bring those practices into your own home and collections. 

Registrants can sign up for a multiday workshop led by leading needle artists, learn more about our fantastic collections, and discover ways you can begin your own journeys of making and collecting.

Designed for a variety of audiences, Winterthur welcomes seasoned embroiderers, collectors, and those curious and eager to learn more. This conference draws its theme from an exhibit of the same name.

About the Exhibit

Stitched in Place, on view through April 4, 2027, explores how American needlework has and continues to serve as a medium for expressing identity, belonging, and awareness of place. Featuring approximately twenty objects from Winterthur’s collection, including  samplers, needlework pictures, hatchments, tools, garments, accessories, and furnishing textiles from the seventeenth through twentieth centuries, this installation invites reflection on how makers used needle and thread to communicate who they were, where they came from, and how they wished to be seen.

Stitched in Place is presented as part of Winterthur’s ongoing Conversations with Collections series in the Galleries.

event.title: Winterthur Institute
event.description:
April 4–16, 2027

Intended for professionals in the care of cultural heritage, graduate students, and scholars of American decorative arts, this two-week immersive experience includes lectures, hands-on workshops, research opportunities, and access to the specialists, gardens, and historic architecture of Winterthur.

Participants will be part of a select cohort that engages in daily study of Winterthur’s world-renowned collection, with contextualization in the history of American decorative arts, object materiality, and techniques of museum stewardship. Upon completion of Winterthur Institute, participants will have gained:

  • historical knowledge of the decorative arts, as well as techniques of cultural analysis, which define the relationship of an object to its time.
  • competency in best practices for handling objects, as demonstrated in a preventive conservation practicum with Winterthur’s collections.
  • an understanding of “sense of place” while studying collections in the former du Pont historic home and estate.
  • 70 hours of professional development in key skills and knowledge for cultural heritage study.
  • support of the Winterthur learning community and a stronger professional network.
  • a certificate of completion.
For more information and to apply, visit winterthurinstitute.org.
Winterthur Institute is supported by Learning Times, LLC; The Decorative Arts Trust; and Winterthur Institute alumni.

event.title: A Bizarre Victorian Bazaar: An Exhibition of Oddities and the Obscure
event.description:
Our outdoor event, A Bizarre Victorian Bazaar: An Exhibition of Oddities and the Obscure, will return the Victoria Mansion this fall!  This one-day fair kicks off the Halloween season with an educational (and entertaining!) take on Victorian folklore, customs, Spiritualism, and more.

Learn about poison books and wallpaper, how purported mediums conducted seances, and why some elite Victorians held mummy unwrapping parties. Have your cards or runes read, create Victorian crafts, and much, much more! This fair will have activities and games for kids throughout the day. Plus, a visit from “Dracula,” music by One-Eared Cat, and readings from “penny dreadfuls.” We’ll also have Sullivan House Bakery onsite for visitors who want to grab a bite to eat while they enjoy demonstrations and performances on the lawn.

Exhibitors and performers include:

  • Phillips Puppets
  • Osher Map Library
  • Portland Ballet
  • Andrew Harris
  • Saco Museum’s Cabinet of Curiosities
  • …and more!

This event is designed for visitors ages 8 and up. We encourage caregiver discretion for younger and more sensitive children.

Keep an eye on our Events webpage, and our Facebook and Instagram pages in the coming weeks as we announce more. A full schedule of events will be available onsite on the day of the event, and a preliminary schedule of events will be available closer to the event date.

Tickets:

Adults: $21
College Students: $8
Children ages 6-17: $6
Children 5 and under: Free
Victoria Mansion Members: Free
Museums for All (SNAP/EBT cardholders): $3 (with valid SNAP/EBT card at check-in)

event.title: Ghostly Bangor Walking Tour
event.description:
The Bangor Historical Society’s Ghostly Bangor Walking Tour features tales of unsolved mysteries, murder, and energies that may still linger in the Queen City. Tours stroll through the streets of Downtown Bangor and last around 90 minutes. Tickets are $12.

Advanced ticketing is required. Our tours are capped at 25 guests, and tickets sell out quickly. Tickets must be purchased by noon of the date of the tour. To purchase tickets or for more info please visit our website or e-mail us at curator@bangorhistoricalsociety.org.

Tours depart from the Bangor Historical Society’s Thomas A. Hill House (159 Union Street, Bangor) at 7 p.m. Parking is available on High Street.

A note on inclement weather: tours will be cancelled if there is a chance of thunderstorms but not if only rain is in the forecast.

event.title: Liberty & Legacy: BHS Annual Awards Night
event.description:
Saturday, October 3 | 6:00–9:00 PM
Penobscot Valley Country Club
366 Main Street, Orono

Join the Bangor Historical Society for Liberty & Legacy: BHS Annual Awards Night, an evening celebrating those who have made a lasting impact on our community and its history, while commemorating the 250th anniversary of the United States and the Declaration of Independence.

Guests are invited to embrace the spirit of the evening by dressing in patriotic colors or as a favorite historical figure. The celebration will include a buffet-style dinner, the presentation of the Bangor Historical Society’s annual awards, and a special opportunity to experience a remarkable piece of American history.

2026 Award Honorees

George Hale
Judge John E. Godfrey Eye Witness to History Award

Bangor Savings Bank
Founding Fathers Preservation & Stewardship Award

Michael Pullen, AIA, LEED AP, Artifex Architects & Engineers
Nelson E. Durgin Generations of Service Award

In honor of this historic milestone, the Bangor Historical Society’s rare William Stone engraving of the Declaration of Independence will make a special trip to Orono and be on display for guests during the evening.

Tickets

Individual: $75
Couple: $140
Table of 8: $560

We hope you’ll join us on October 3 for a memorable evening celebrating history, preservation, service, and the people who help keep our shared stories alive.

Thank you to our sponsors:  Cross Insurance & The City of Bangor.

event.title: Darker Mount Hope Cemetery Tour October 23rd
event.description:
Explore Bangor’s dark side and take a walk amid the shadows during the Bangor Historical Society’s Darker Mount Hope Cemetery Tour, Friday and Saturday, October 23 & 24, 2026.

As the night deepens while you meander the paved paths, a cast of living souls will regale you with dramatic, moving, touching, mysterious, and even spooky stories —sprinkled with a bit of history, of course— about the permanent residents of Mount Hope. This nighttime walking tour of one of the oldest garden cemeteries in the country is a seasonal favorite.

Tours are conducted on foot and are no more than one mile, but may include stairs, hills, and uneven terrain. We recommend sturdy footwear, warm clothing, and a flashlight. Tours are conducted rain or shine.

Advanced Tickets are required and are sold for specific start times, starting at 6 pm.

Tickets will go on sale to the public on Thursday, September 24th, at noon.

Guests should enter Mount Hope Cemetery at 1048 State Street, Bangor, and check in near the Superintendent’s Lodge at no sooner than 20 minutes before their departure time. Parking is available along both sides of the cemetery entry road, accessible via the State Street gate.

Use “Second Maine Regiment Memorial” into GPS for the correct entrance gate location.

Direct questions to the museum curator via email at curator@bangorhistoricalsociety.org or by calling 207-942-1900.

event.title: History in Focus:  The Brady Gang Shootout
event.description:
Join us for a one-time only event on Saturday, October 24th at 10am.

The morning will begin with a meeting inside the Thomas A. Hill House, where we will examine photos and artifacts related to the FBI’s most wanted gangster in 1937. We will follow Al Brady and his gang and learn of the crimes that led to their eventual demise on Central Street on that bright October morning in 1937. Following the talk, we will walk to the site of the shooting to see where history happened 89 years ago.

We have a limited number of tickets available for this special event at $20 per ticket.

Ball & Chain presents

Matine Cubana

with DJ Danis LaClave & Friends

4:00pm – 8:00pm

Sundays during the day, Ball & Chain transforms into one of Little Havana’s liveliest daytime destinations with Matine Cubana, a weekly celebration of Cuban music, cocktails, dancing, and Miami culture in the heart of Calle Ocho. Held every Sunday, Matine Cubana brings together locals and visitors for an energetic afternoon filled with live Latin music, tropical drinks, delicious Cuban food, and the unmistakable atmosphere that has made Little Havana famous around the world.

Mambo Mondays

presented by Carlos Saoco

9:00pm – 12:00am

Set by DJ Iván
Free Salsa & Bachata Class @9pm

21+ With Proper Identification

________________________________________

Mambo Mondays is the night Miami’s salsa community claims for itself. The week is just starting, the tourist Saturdays are five days off, and the room fills with people who came to dance. By 8:30 the patio crowd has finished dinner and started drifting toward the floor. By 9pm, Carlos Saoco is on the floor and the night’s DJ is queuing up the music that runs until 1am.

Set by DJ Vila

BachaTuesdays is the night Ball & Chain hands over to bachata. The room shifts when the music does, and the room knows the difference. By 8:30 the patio crowd is finishing dinner and the floor is starting to settle into the night.
